source_user: A service receives a mix of short prompts and long generations. Design an evaluation plan that reports TTFT, TPOT, throughput, queueing, and P99 latency. Scenario variant 204: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: separate prefill and decode behavior; fix workload distribution; report warmup; use repeated trials; capture GPU memory and request-level traces.
corrected_answer: Assumptions and definitions: treat arrival, queue admission, service start, prefill completion, first-token, each decode-token, completion, cancellation, error, and timeout as synchronized request events. Define TTFT as arrival-to-first-token, queueing as arrival-to-service-start, TPOT as inter-token time after the first token (report its median and tail, not only a mean), and throughput as completed requests/s and output-tokens/s; state whether client/network time is included and use ms, s, requests/s, and tokens/s. Separate prefill work from decode work and report prompt and generated-token lengths. Falsifiable hypothesis: under a fixed seeded mix of short prompts and long generations and the same offered load, the candidate prefill/decode-aware policy reduces P99 TTFT and TPOT versus the baseline below the point where queueing or GPU-memory pressure causes saturation; reject the claim if confidence intervals overlap the baseline or any guardrail regresses. Use a replayable arrival trace with predeclared length distributions, concurrency, model/version, tokenizer, hardware, batching, sampling, cache/admission policy, and load levels. Warm up identically, exclude or report warmup separately, randomize or interleave baseline and treatment, and repeat enough independent trials to estimate uncertainty. Capture synchronized per-request and per-token traces plus prefill/decode phase times, queue depth, completions, cancellations, errors, timeouts, correctness checks, GPU utilization/clocks, allocated/reserved/peak memory, OOM/retry events, and host/network telemetry. Report counts, success rate, throughput, queue time, TTFT, TPOT, end-to-end P50/P95/P99, phase- and length-stratified results, confidence intervals, and raw-trace provenance. Control or measure cache state, thermal/power clocks, batching effects, background load, network/client overhead, scheduler version, tokenization, run order, and trace-clock skew; do not infer causality if these differ. Predeclare SLO and safety gates: stop or roll back on OOM, correctness mismatch, elevated error/timeout rate, unsafe isolation behavior, or a material P99/SLO regression; preserve logs and avoid production exposure until canary evidence supports it. Estimates must be labeled, and platform-specific conclusions require measured evidence.
risks: percentile instability or insufficient samples
workload, cache, batching, thermal, or run-order confounding
GPU memory pressure, OOM, and admission instability
timestamp or trace synchronization error
limited generalization beyond the measured platform
evidence_required: raw synchronized request and token traces
repeated randomized or interleaved baseline/treatment trials
GPU memory, utilization, clock, and queue telemetry
correctness, error, timeout, and SLO results
predeclared rollback thresholds and canary results
